entries.name: Settlement.Org
entries.description: Settlement.Org is an information website for newcomers to Ontario from the Ontario Council of Agencies Serving Immigrants (OCASI). It answers common questions about immigration, housing, health, work, school and daily life, and has a 'Find Services Near Me' search by region.
entries.cost_note: Its 'What are settlement services?' page says settlement services 'are free and are always confidential'. No fee is shown for using the site.
entries.evidence: If you are new to Ontario, you can find answers to common questions about your new home on Settlement.Org
entries.notes: Also has translated information, an 'Ask a Question' discussion forum and Orientation to Ontario webinars. French version: Etablissement.Org.

entries.name: Find free newcomer services near you (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada)
entries.description: A Government of Canada search tool that lists settlement services funded by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC). You can search by postal code or city and filter by service type, language, online or in-person service, and groups such as persons with disabilities.
entries.cost_note: The page says 'You can get our free settlement services if you’re eligible'.
entries.evidence: We fund many qualified professionals who can help you successfully adapt to life in Canada. You can get our free settlement services if you’re eligible
entries.notes: National tool (does not list providers in Quebec). Eligible: permanent residents including resettled refugees, people approved in principle for permanent residence, protected persons, and some temporary residents and pathways. From April 1, 2026, economic class permanent residents can only access newcomer services for a limited time. Links to pre-arrival services for people outside Canada.

entries.name: 211 Ontario
entries.description: 211 is a free and confidential helpline that connects people in Ontario to social and community services and programs. Its Community Navigators ask questions to understand your needs and refer you to the right supports.
entries.cost_note: The About page says '211 is a free and confidential service'.
entries.evidence: 211 is a free and confidential service that easily connects people to the critical social and community supports they need.
entries.notes: Contact page: phone answered by real people 24/7 in 150+ languages; text 2-1-1 is available 24/7; live chat and email Monday to Friday 7am-9pm ET. Also available by online search. The About page says 211 will also advocate on a contact's behalf at their request. Settlement.Org suggests calling 211 to find the settlement agency closest to you. 211's newcomer topic pages were behind a bot check and could not be read.

entries.name: Get settled in Ontario (Government of Ontario)
entries.description: The Government of Ontario's guide to moving to and settling in Ontario, with a search to find a settlement agency near you. Settlement agencies can help you find housing, a job or childcare, register children in school, and get information about healthcare and social services.
entries.cost_note: The page says settlement agency services 'are free and are available in multiple languages in communities across Ontario'.
entries.evidence: These services are free and are available in multiple languages in communities across Ontario.
entries.notes: Also covers health cards, driver's licences, public transit (including transportation services for people with disabilities) and services in French. The page says French-speaking newcomers are eligible for all provincial settlement services.

entries.name: S.P.L.A.S.H. (Settlement Program Learning Abilities Service Hub), Learning Disabilities Association of Toronto District
entries.description: A settlement program of the Learning Disabilities Association of Toronto District that offers newcomers one-on-one settlement support, group workshops, language support and connections to community services. It aims to help newcomers with language accommodation and learning styles.
entries.cost_note: The page says S.P.L.A.S.H. 'provides FREE settlement information and orientation services & programs to newcomers'.
entries.address: 121 Willowdale Avenue, Toronto, ON M2N 6A3
entries.evidence: Provide assistance to newcomers with language accommodation and learning styles
entries.notes: Eligibility listed: permanent residents, Convention refugees and other IRCC-eligible groups. Help includes IRCC applications, benefits (OHIP, SIN, ODSP and more), housing benefits, employment counselling, tax clinic referrals and extra English support. Address is the head office on the contact page (the Settlement Office is there in Units 203-204); phone and email are the Settlement Office's. A client testimonial describes support for a newcomer with a learning disability.

entries.name: SAAAC Autism Centre
entries.description: SAAAC Autism Centre supports individuals with autism, their caregivers and families with culturally responsive services. It began by serving South Asian families in the Greater Toronto Area and now also serves diverse newcomer communities.
entries.cost_note: The pages fetched do not list fees.
entries.address: 705 Progress Ave Unit 63, Scarborough, Ontario M1H 2X1
entries.evidence: As our Centre grew, we began providing services to diverse newcomer communities.
entries.notes: Programs on the home page include ABA therapy and SAAAC CARES, a caregiver support program. A second site is the Birchmount Campus, 1870 Birchmount Road, Scarborough. Head office address, phone and email are from the contact page.

entries.name: Employment Services for Deaf Newcomers, Bob Rumball Centre
entries.description: An employment program for Deaf adult newcomers to Canada, with an employment counsellor and workshops on resumes, cover letters and interview techniques. ASL/English interpreters help clients take part fully in workshops and interviews.
entries.cost_note: The page says the program is funded by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada but does not state fees.
entries.address: 2395 Bayview Ave., North York, ON, M2L 1A2
entries.evidence: Empowering Deaf adult newcomers to Canada, our Employment Services program offers tailored support to navigate the job market.
entries.notes: A newcomer service for people with a disability (Deaf). Bob Rumball also offers LINC and LBS adult education for newcomers and Deaf adults. TTY: 416-449-2728.

entries.name: COSTI Immigrant Services
entries.description: COSTI helps newcomers in the Greater Toronto Area find a job, learn English and settle into a new home. Its team speaks over 60 languages, with 17 offices across the GTA and online support.
entries.cost_note: The pages fetched do not say whether services are free.
entries.evidence: COSTI has 17 offices across the Greater Toronto Area and also offers online support, so you can get help wherever you are.
entries.notes: Services include employment, housing and settlement help, English language training, skills training, counselling and mental health supports, and a Translation and Interpretation Bureau. Phone and email are from the contact page (corporate office, Toronto M6E 3P2; street address not printed).

entries.name: ACCES Employment
entries.description: ACCES Employment helps jobseekers facing employment barriers, including newcomers, enter the Canadian job market. It offers employment and bridging programs, mentoring, pre-arrival programs and help starting a business.
entries.cost_note: The home page says 'most of our services are free'.
entries.evidence: We assist thousands of jobseekers facing employment barriers to enter the Canadian job market, and most of our services are free.
entries.notes: Locations: Toronto, North York, Scarborough, Markham, Mississauga, Newmarket and Brampton. Registered charity (A.C.C.E.S.) Accessible Community Counselling and Employment Services. Has a Refugee Hub and a Youth Hub. Phone from the contact page.

entries.name: YMCA of Greater Toronto, Immigrant Services
entries.description: YMCA Immigrant Services in the Greater Toronto Area offer English and French classes, information sessions about your new community, and settlement advice. Programs include the Newcomer Information Centre, language assessment and referral, the Newcomer Youth Leadership Development program and Next Stop Canada pre-arrival services.
entries.cost_note: The page says these services are 'all free!' and that language assessments for government-funded programs are 'at no cost'.
entries.evidence: Learn or improve your English and French, attend information sessions to get to know your new community better, get settlement advice and assistance; all free!
entries.notes: The Barrett YMCA Centre for Newcomers to Canada is at 365 Bloor St E, 18th floor, Unit 1800A, Toronto (its location page gives 416-925-5462 for booking language assessments). info@newcomersincanada.ca is for online service questions. Next Stop Canada gives online pre-arrival help to eligible people living overseas.

entries.name: Catholic Crosscultural Services (CCS)
entries.description: CCS has helped immigrants and refugees since 1959, with free services for newcomers from learning English to finding jobs. Settlement staff help in over 30 languages, online and in person.
entries.cost_note: The home page says 'we offer free services ranging from learning English to finding jobs for all newcomers'.
entries.address: 55 Town Centre Court, Suite 401, Scarborough M1P 4X4
entries.evidence: we offer free services ranging from learning English to finding jobs for all newcomers
entries.notes: Also offers the Refugee Sponsorship Training Program (RSTP), housing support, women's support services, youth support and newcomer wellbeing support. Address printed under 'About us' on the home page. cathcrosscultural.org now redirects to ccscan.ca.

entries.name: CultureLink Settlement and Community Services
entries.description: CultureLink is a settlement and community organization in Toronto that helps newcomers to Canada settle into their communities. Services include a Newcomer Settlement Program, settlement workers in schools, mentorship and brief mental health counselling.
entries.cost_note: The home page lists some free programs: up to eight free 45-minute counselling sessions and a free three-day Newcomer Orientation Week for high school students. Fees for other programs are not stated.
entries.address: 2340 Dundas Street West, Suite 301 [Crossways Mall] Toronto ON M6P 4A9
entries.evidence: We help newcomers to Canada settle into their communities.
entries.notes: Its Newcomer Settlement Program page says the program 'is open to all newcomers, regardless of your settlement status'. Open Monday to Friday, 10 am to 6 pm.

entries.name: Toronto Public Library: New to Canada
entries.description: Toronto Public Library's services for newcomers to Canada, including library materials in many languages and English learning resources. You can meet with a settlement worker who can help you get started in Toronto and Canada.
entries.cost_note: The page does not state costs.
entries.evidence: Meet with a settlement worker who can help you get started in Toronto and Canada.
entries.notes: Also has library information in over 40 languages, a practice Citizenship Test, and online tools for English learning and IELTS practice.

entries.name: Moving to Toronto (City of Toronto)
entries.description: The City of Toronto's page for people thinking about moving to Toronto or who have just arrived, with information for before and after you arrive. It points newcomers to settlement workers and a Newcomer Welcome Brochure.
entries.cost_note: Information page; no costs stated.
entries.evidence: Whether you’re just thinking about moving to Toronto or already making plans, you’ll find the information you need right here.
entries.notes: 311 Toronto (https://www.toronto.ca/home/311-toronto-at-your-service/) gives access to non-emergency City services, programs and information 24 hours a day, seven days a week, in more than 180 languages. The page also offers 'Indigenous Peoples in Toronto: An Introduction for Newcomers'.

entries.name: Ottawa Community Immigrant Services Organization (OCISO)
entries.description: OCISO supports immigrants and refugees in Ottawa with settlement services, English classes, job mentoring, counselling, youth programs and community connections. It serves about 10,000 people a year in over 50 languages.
entries.cost_note: The home page says 'OCISO offers free Language Instruction for Newcomers to Canada (LINC)'. Fees for other services are not stated.
entries.address: 275 rue Bay Street, Ottawa, ON K1R 5Z5
entries.evidence: Our newcomer settlement services provide support while you and your family adapt to your new life in Canada.
entries.notes: Address is 'OCISO Main/Principal' on the home page; other offices are at 959 Wellington Street West (walk-in services Monday to Thursday) and 1800 Bank Street. Counselling specializes in survivors of war, torture, trauma, political persecution and imprisonment. YOCISO programs serve immigrant youth ages 13 to 24. Also runs an income tax clinic and homework club.

entries.name: Catholic Centre for Immigrants Ottawa (CCI Ottawa)
entries.description: CCI has helped newcomers to Ottawa settle, grow and feel connected for more than seventy years, with programs and resources to help them build their lives. It serves permanent residents, refugees and refugee claimants living in Ottawa.
entries.cost_note: The home page does not state fees.
entries.address: 219 Argyle Avenue, Ottawa ON, K2P 2H4
entries.evidence: CCI provides tailored support for newcomers in Ottawa, including permanent residents, refugees and refugee claimants.
entries.notes: CCI serves Ottawa residents only; people living in Gatineau are pointed to Gatineau settlement services. The home page reports housing support and full-time jobs secured with CCI's help.

entries.name: Newcomer Centre of Peel (NCP)
entries.description: Newcomer Centre of Peel is a settlement agency for new immigrants to Canada, with English classes, employment services, help starting a business, settlement counselling and community connections. It serves recent immigrants, refugees and international students in the Peel region.
entries.cost_note: The page says 'all of our programs and services are 100% free for newcomers to Canada'.
entries.address: 165 Dundas Street West, Suite 116. Mississauga, ON L5B 2N6
entries.evidence: Thanks to our funders, all of our programs and services are 100% free for newcomers to Canada
entries.notes: Office is wheelchair accessible (ramps, elevators and automated doors). Bring your PR card to your first visit to get services at no cost. Open Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm; in-person and online classes and appointments, including evening classes.

entries.name: Peel Multicultural Council (PMC)
entries.description: PMC's information, assessment and orientation services help newcomers in Peel Region adapt and reach their goals, including a personalized settlement plan, help with forms and links to resources. Services are offered in English, French, Arabic, Chinese, Hindi, Punjabi, Spanish, Tagalog and Urdu.
entries.cost_note: The page lists a Free Income Tax Clinic; fees for settlement services are not stated.
entries.address: 6630 Turner Valley Rd, Mississauga, ON L5N 2P1
entries.evidence: The Information, Assessment and Orientation services at PMC aim to provide newcomers with all the assistance and resources they need to adapt to their surroundings
entries.notes: Eligibility documents listed include a Confirmation of Permanent Residence, an IRB decision accepting a refugee claim, or a citizenship card, passport, study permit or post-graduate work permit (naturalized citizens and international students can receive limited settlement services). Address from the contact page.

entries.name: Building Multicultural Communities (BMC)
entries.description: BMC provides settlement services to newcomers to Canada, with personalized guidance, practical information, community resources and individual support. Help covers healthcare, education, employment and government services.
entries.cost_note: Orientation to Ontario workshops are described as free; fees for other services are not stated.
entries.evidence: BMC provides various types of settlement services to newcomers to Canada, supporting them through their transition
entries.notes: Listed by the Government of Ontario as Brampton Multicultural Community Centre. Locations page lists offices in Brampton (44 Peel Centre Drive, 263 Queen Street East, 197 County Court Blvd and 40 Peel Centre Drive), Mississauga (4120 Ridgeway Drive) and Milton. Also runs settlement workers in schools and libraries, employment, youth, mental health and seniors services.

entries.name: Welcome Centre Immigrant Services
entries.description: Welcome Centres in York Region and Durham Region bring settlement help, English classes, job support, accreditation help and interpretation together in one place. They help in person or by phone, email or video.
entries.cost_note: The FAQ mentions a free income tax return service for registered clients and says document translation is not free; other fees are not stated.
entries.evidence: At Welcome Centre Immigrant Services, you can find all the services you need in one place.
entries.notes: Also serves Durham Region. Locations: Ajax, Markham North, Markham South, Newmarket, Oshawa/Clarington, Pickering, Richmond Hill and Vaughan, plus a Mobile Outreach Unit for York Region and Simcoe County. The home page lists general information lines in 18 languages.

entries.name: Newcomer Services (York Region)
entries.description: York Region's page for people moving to a new country or region, with a Newcomer Guide on settling in, transit, housing, health care, school, work and local government. It also describes the Welcome Centres that help immigrants settle.
entries.cost_note: Information page; no costs stated.
entries.address: 17250 Yonge St, Newmarket, ON L3Y 6Z1
entries.evidence: York Region has developed a Newcomer Guide that provides useful information to help you and your family settle in York Region quickly and easily.
entries.notes: Phone and address are York Region's general inquiries contact printed on the page. The Local Immigration Partnership has recorded webinars for newcomers.

entries.name: Durham Immigration (Durham Local Immigration Partnership)
entries.description: The Region of Durham's immigration website for people moving to Durham Region, with a map of settlement services and links to the Durham Welcome Centres. It also covers driving, work and study, translation and the Durham Local Immigration Partnership.
entries.cost_note: Information website; no costs stated.
entries.address: 605 Rossland Rd. E., P.O. Box 623, Whitby, ON L1N 6A3
entries.evidence: There are lots of resources to help you get settled in Durham Region.
entries.notes: The site says almost 30% of Durham's residents are immigrants.

entries.name: YMCA Hamilton | Burlington | Brantford, Immigrant Services
entries.description: YMCA Immigrant Services connects newcomers and their families with services such as health care, education and language help, with staff who speak a variety of languages. Services include newcomer information and orientation and English language assessments in the Hamilton and Grand Erie regions.
entries.cost_note: The page says 'Free help and support to help you get settled in Canada' and offers 'FREE, in-person and online, English language assessments'.
entries.evidence: Free help and support to help you get settled in Canada.
entries.notes: YMCA Immigrant Services - Hamilton is at 25 Main Street West (905-526-8452); Stoney Creek is at 211 Centennial Parkway North (905-662-9400); there is also a Brantford location. Eligibility includes permanent residents, Convention refugees and protected persons, people approved in principle, and some caregiver and provincial nominee program participants. Funded by IRCC.

entries.name: Newcomer Learning Centre (Hamilton Public Library)
entries.description: The Newcomer Learning Centre at Hamilton's Central Library has materials for English learners and tutors, English tutoring, conversation circles and information sessions on topics such as employment and tenant rights. The page also points to local language assessment and settlement services.
entries.cost_note: The page does not state fees. Registration is required, and proof of permanent residency or protected person status is requested.
entries.evidence: Practice English with a tutor in-person, online or both.
entries.notes: On the 4th floor of Central Library. Tutoring needs language benchmarks of 3 or higher in all skills.

entries.name: London Cross Cultural Learner Centre (CCLC)
entries.description: The CCLC supports newcomers and their families in London with settlement, language, employment and community connection services. It focuses on Government Assisted Refugees, refugee claimants and other vulnerable newcomers.
entries.cost_note: Settlement service fees are not stated; interpretation and translation are paid services ('Competitive pricing').
entries.address: 505 Dundas Street, London, Ontario N6B 1W4
entries.evidence: We support newcomers and their families as they build their lives in Canada, providing services that help people settle, connect and succeed.
entries.notes: Also offers settlement workers in schools (SWIS), language assessment (including for the Windsor-Essex region), and interpretation and certified translation in 80+ languages. Contact details are from the home page.

entries.name: Reception House Waterloo Region
entries.description: Reception House welcomes and supports refugees and high-needs newcomers in Waterloo Region through settlement, housing and integration services. Services include the Resettlement Assistance Program, case management for newcomers with complex needs, employment services and youth programs.
entries.cost_note: The page does not state fees.
entries.address: Suite 700 - 101 Frederick St, Kitchener, ON N2H 6R2
entries.evidence: Reception House Waterloo Region is a non-profit, community-based organization that welcomes and supports refugees and high-needs newcomers through settlement, housing, and integration services
entries.notes: Client Support Services include healthcare navigation and advocacy for refugees with complex needs. Open Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM - 4:30 PM.

entries.name: Immigration Waterloo Region (Waterloo Region Immigration Partnership)
entries.description: Immigration Waterloo Region brings together the information immigrants need to settle, work and belong in Waterloo Region, including settlement resources and organizations that can help. It does not provide direct services; it points to partner agencies that do.
entries.cost_note: Information website; no costs stated.
entries.evidence: Immigration Waterloo Region brings together the information immigrants, employers, and partners need to help newcomers settle, work, and belong in our region.
entries.notes: The site says: 'We do not provide direct services to immigrants.' It speaks to people new to the region as well as new to Canada.

entries.name: The Multicultural Council of Windsor and Essex County (MCC)
entries.description: The MCC's Newcomer Settlement Program offers one-on-one settlement and orientation help, information about community and government services, referrals, and workshops. The MCC also runs the Windsor Resettlement Assistance Program for Government Assisted Refugees.
entries.cost_note: The page does not state fees.
entries.address: 245 Janette Ave, Windsor, ON N9A 4Z2
entries.evidence: The Newcomer Settlement Program helps our clients become involved in all aspects of life in Ontario.
entries.notes: Address is the Downtown Windsor office; an East End office is at 7651 Tecumseh Rd E (home page). Client Support Services give up to one year of case management to Government Assisted Refugees. Settlement services are delivered in partnership with the YMCA of Southwestern Ontario and Women's Enterprise Skills Training of Windsor Inc.

entries.name: Immigrant Services Kingston and Area (ISKA), Kingston Community Health Centres
entries.description: ISKA, a program of Kingston Community Health Centres, offers settlement support for immigrants, newcomers and refugees, including help with government documents, finding a home, enrolling children in school and language assessment. It also runs groups such as English circles and meetups for newcomer women.
entries.cost_note: Settlement fees are not stated. KCHC's newcomer page says language assessments are free for eligible clients; translation services are paid.
entries.address: 837 Princess St. Suite 201, Kingston, Ontario K7L 1G9
entries.evidence: We accompany you along your settlement journey and help make your transition as smooth as possible.
entries.notes: Languages: English, French, Hindi, Urdu, Creole, Arabic, Spanish, Turkish, Portuguese, Mandarin and Indonesian. Wheelchair accessible. Newcomers who arrived in Kingston within the past year (temporary workers or permanent residents) can get a welcome package with transit and recreation passes, while supplies last. KCHC also runs a newcomer bridging health clinic.

entries.name: YMCA of Northeastern Ontario, Immigrant Services
entries.description: YMCA Immigrant Services helps newcomers settle in the Greater Sudbury region. Multilingual settlement staff help you build a personalized settlement plan and refer you to other services.
entries.cost_note: The page does not state fees.
entries.evidence: YMCA’s Immigrant Services has been helping Newcomers settle into the Greater Sudbury region for more than 10 years.
entries.notes: The phone number is given in the French section of the page. The page links to French-language settlement services and language training.

entries.name: Thunder Bay Multicultural Association (TBMA)
entries.description: TBMA helps newcomers settle in Thunder Bay with Orientation to Ontario, English classes (LINC), language assessment, the Resettlement Assistance Program, an Employment Connector and citizenship preparation classes.
entries.cost_note: The page does not state fees.
entries.address: 17 N. Court Street, Thunder Bay, Ontario, P7A 4T4
entries.evidence: New to Canada or Thunder Bay?
entries.notes: Toll-free 1-866-831-1141; open Monday to Friday 9am - 4:30pm (contact page). Also runs a 'Stay In The Bay' Newcomer Welcome Day and community interpreter training. tbma.ca redirects to thunderbay.org.

entries.name: New Canadians Centre Peterborough
entries.description: The New Canadians Centre provides free, confidential services to immigrants and refugees in the Peterborough, Kawartha Lakes, Haliburton and Northumberland regions, including settlement information, English language assessment, settlement workers in schools, employment and community connections.
entries.cost_note: The page says 'We provide free and confidential services to immigrants and refugees'.
entries.address: 221 Romaine Street, Peterborough, Ontario K9J 2C3
entries.evidence: We provide free and confidential services to immigrants and refugees living in the Peterborough, Kawartha Lakes, Haliburton or Northumberland regions.
entries.notes: Offices in Peterborough, Northumberland (co-located at Watton Employment Services) and City of Kawartha Lakes; appointments by phone, email, video and in person (contact page). New clients should book an intake appointment and bring immigration documents.

entries.name: YMCA of Simcoe/Muskoka, Immigrant Services
entries.description: YMCA Immigrant Services in Barrie gives eligible newcomers English language training and settlement services, including needs assessment, orientation, information and referral, and labour market information. Its International Student Connect program offers online and in-person support to international students in Ontario.
entries.cost_note: The pages do not state fees; the services are supported by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada.
entries.address: 320 Bayfield Street, Suite 63A, Barrie ON, L4M 3C1
entries.evidence: YMCA Immigrant Services ensures eligible newcomers to Canada receive appropriate English language training and settlement services including assessment of needs, orientation, information and referral
entries.notes: International Student Connect (https://www.ymcaofsimcoemuskoka.ca/programs-services/immigrant-services/international-student-connect/) is for people who have applied to, or are thinking about studying at, a college or university in Ontario. Address, phone and email are from the Immigrant Services locations page.

entries.name: Bridges Niagara (formerly Niagara Folk Arts Multicultural Centre)
entries.description: Bridges Niagara offers settlement and resettlement services for immigrants and refugees in Niagara, including settlement help, employment support, English classes (LINC and ESL), community connections, youth programs and newcomer wellness support.
entries.cost_note: The page says Bridges Niagara 'provides a variety of free settlement and resettlement services to assist all immigrants and refugees'.
entries.address: 85 Church Street, St. Catharines, ON L2R 3C7
entries.evidence: Bridges Niagara provides a variety of free settlement and resettlement services to assist all immigrants and refugees.
entries.notes: folk-arts.ca now says 'Niagara Folk Arts Multicultural Centre is now Bridges Niagara!' and redirects there. Also runs the Resettlement Assistance Program for government-assisted refugees and a pilot program for migrant workers. Contact details are from the home page.

entries.name: Immigrant Services Guelph-Wellington (ISGW)
entries.description: ISGW offers settlement services to help immigrants take part fully in Canadian life, including orientation, referrals, advocacy, settlement workers in schools, language assessment, and interpretation and translation. It serves newcomers in Guelph and Wellington County.
entries.cost_note: The pages do not state fees.
entries.address: 104 Dawson Rd. Unit 102, Guelph, ON N1H 1A6
entries.evidence: We offer settlement services to help immigrants participate fully in Canadian life.
entries.notes: Services are available in person, by phone and by video chat (contact page). Counsellors can help with documents after arrival, benefits, PR cards, citizenship, housing support and employment counselling, and can help families apply to the Free to Grow Program, which funds recreation for children and youth 0 to 18 in Guelph and Wellington County.

unverified.name: SISO (Settlement and Integration Services Organization), Hamilton
unverified.reason: sisohamilton.org did not resolve (DNS lookup failed) when fetched on 2026-10-17, and SISO does not appear in IRCC's current service-finder data for Hamilton. No other official page could be found because the web-search budget had run out. Hamilton is covered here by YMCA Immigrant Services and the Hamilton Public Library Newcomer Learning Centre.

unverified.name: Ottawa Public Library, newcomer services
unverified.reason: Could not find a newcomer services page on biblioottawalibrary.ca by direct navigation (guessed URLs returned 404) and web search was unavailable, so it is left out.

unverified.name: 211 Ontario 'Settlement services' topic page (211ontario.ca/211-topics/newcomers/settlement-services)
unverified.reason: The page loads only a bot-verification screen. 211 Ontario is listed instead from its About and Contact pages, which did load.
